summary.text: Charlice Byrd is a Republican state representative from Woodstock who has represented Georgia House District 20 since January 2021 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Jason Tanner.
An educator by profession, she also held the District 20 seat from 2005 to 2013, according to Ballotpedia.

paragraphs.text: Byrd lives in Woodstock, Georgia, and earned a B.A. in elementary education from Southeastern Louisiana University.
Her career experience includes working with Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. and as an educator.
Ballotpedia lists Byrd as having held House District 20 from 2005 to 2013 and as having been defeated by Michael Caldwell in the July 31, 2012 Republican primary.

She returned to the race in 2020, defeating Rick Ballew, Jessica Long and Jordan Ridley in the June 9, 2020 Republican primary and Katrina Singletary in the August 11 runoff, and then defeated Ginny Lennox in the general election.
She took office on January 11, 2021, and was re-elected in 2022 and 2024; in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary she defeated Mark Fernandez.

For the 2025-2026 session she was assigned to the Budget and Fiscal Affairs Oversight, Economic Development and Tourism, Game, Fish, and Parks, Human Relations and Aging, Judiciary - Non-Civil, State Planning and Community Affairs, and Transportation committees.
